review_candidates.description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior VFX Engineer based in Germany. This is a senior individual contributor role focused on the technology and runtime systems that power real-time visual effects in a major Unity3D game project. You will work at the intersection of VFX, Technical Art, Rendering, and Engineering, turning creative concepts into scalable and production-ready solutions. The role combines shader development, particle systems, GPU-driven effects, runtime architecture, tooling, and performance optimization. You will have significant technical ownership, from rapid prototyping and architectural decisions through to production implementation. Working closely with artists and engineers, you will help balance visual ambition with performance, scalability, and maintainability. This is an opportunity to directly shape the technology that enables high-quality real-time effects across a large game. Design and implement shaders using HLSL, Shader Graph, Amplify, or comparable technologies. Build and optimize particle-based effects using mesh particles, trails, flipbooks, procedural techniques, and GPU-driven approaches. Create artist-facing Unity tools, including custom inspectors, validators, asset processors, batch workflows, and reusable production utilities. Optimize VFX for mobile and other performance-constrained platforms, with a focus on GPU performance, memory usage, overdraw, shader complexity, and runtime efficiency. Collaborate closely with VFX Artists, Technical Artists, Gameplay Engineers, and Rendering Engineers to translate creative requirements into robust technical solutions. Prototype new rendering and VFX approaches, validate their technical feasibility, and bring successful solutions through to production. Establish reusable templates, workflows, documentation, and technical standards that improve the efficiency and consistency of the wider VFX team. Proven experience shipping particle-based effects in Unity, including Shuriken or equivalent systems. Hands-on experience with mesh particles, trails, flipbooks, shader-driven effects, and procedural VFX techniques. Strong C# programming skills, ideally within gameplay, engine, or performance-critical systems. Experience with ECS/DOTS, Jobs, Burst, or equivalent performance-oriented architectures is strongly preferred. Strong understanding of mobile GPU optimization, including overdraw, half precision, texture and memory budgets, shader variants, and runtime constraints. Experience creating Unity Editor tooling such as custom inspectors, property drawers, asset processors, and batch tools. Understanding of Metal, Vulkan, and GLES, including platform-specific graphics limitations and shader or PSO warmup considerations. Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively across artistic and engineering disciplines. Fluent English. Nice To Have Strong experience with Unity DOTS/Entities, ECS-based rendering, or instanced material properties. Experience with compute shaders and GPU-driven effects. Knowledge of vertex animation techniques, SDFs, procedural noise, and procedural rendering. Experience with procedural or voxel geometry, dynamic meshes, hull generation, or custom lighting systems. Experience developing networked gameplay effects, including predicted versus confirmed events. Background working on multiplayer or large-scale gameplay systems. A strong artistic eye and an ability to contribute to VFX look development. Experience building effects for mobile or other highly performance-constrained platforms. Experience delivering stylized game projects, particularly for mobile platforms. Benefits Meaningful technical ownership over the VFX technology powering a major Unity3D game project. Direct collaboration with experienced VFX Artists, Technical Artists, Rendering Engineers, and Gameplay Engineers. The opportunity to solve complex rendering, performance, and scalability challenges. A role where engineering directly enables creative ambition and visual quality. A highly collaborative international working environment. Fully remote work. review_candidates.description: Job Description Company Description Work with Us. Change the World. At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations. There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world. We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us. Job Description Role Summary The Senior Planning Engineer works within the consultant's project controls team, acting on behalf of the client to oversee the planning and schedule performance of the contractors delivering a multi-contract rail programme in the UAE. The role reviews and accepts contractor programmes, monitors and verifies progress, maintains an integrated programme-level view across all contracts, and provides independent assessment of schedule variances, delays and extension of time claims. The role also gives the client clear, concise and executive-level insight into programme status, critical path and schedule risk. Key Responsibilities Contractor Programme Review and Acceptance Review contractors' baseline programmes for compliance with contract requirements, including key dates, milestones, sectional completion, WBS structure, logic, resource loading and constraints, and recommend acceptance or rejection with clear, documented comments. Review and challenge EPC schedule logic, float use, critical path integrity and durations, making sure programmes are realistic and fit for use in progress monitoring and delay assessment. Review contractors' revised programmes, recovery programmes and monthly updates, making sure changes are properly justified and do not hide delay or float manipulation. Specify and enforce planning requirements, such as WBS, coding structure, update procedures and submission formats, so reporting is consistent across all contracts. Integrated Programme Management Develop and maintain the integrated master programme, combining all contractor programmes with design, authority approvals, third-party works and client-side activities. Identify and manage interfaces and dependencies between contracts (civil, trackwork, rail systems, stations, depots), highlighting cross-contract risks to the critical path early. Assess how delays on one contract affect the others and the overall programme completion date. Progress Monitoring and Verification Independently verify contractor-reported progress through site inspections, measurement records, design deliverable status and procurement tracking. Agree progress measurement methods and rules of credit with contractors and hold them to it. Track schedule performance using Earned Value Management (EVM), including SPI and CPI, earned value, planned value and forecast trends, and relate it to cost and payment performance. Reporting to the Client Prepare weekly and monthly progress reports and presentations for the client, summarising status, key issues, critical path movement, risks and recommended actions at an executive level. Produce programme dashboards, S-curves, milestone trackers and look-ahead summaries across all contracts. Present schedule findings in progress meetings and hold contractors to account for slippage and recovery commitments. Variance, Delay and Claims Assessment Identify and investigate schedule variances, determine root causes, and instruct or request recovery measures from contractors. Independently assess contractors' extension of time (EOT) claims and time impact analyses (TIAs), and prepare the Engineer's assessment. Assess the time effect of variations, instructions and change requests before they are issued, so the client understands the schedule consequences of its decisions. Keep independent schedule records to support the client's position in claims and disputes. Scope and Change Control Support scope control and change management across the programme, making sure approved changes are properly reflected in contractor programmes and the integrated master programme. Interpret drawings, specifications and contract documents to check that contractor programmes reflect the full contracted scope. Qualifications and Experience Bachelor's degree in civil engineering, Construction Management or a related discipline. At least 10 years of planning and scheduling experience on major infrastructure projects. Experience on rail, metro or light rail projects. Advanced proficiency in Primavera P6. Proven experience assessing EOT claims and TIAs, and applying delay analysis methods. Strong working knowledge of FIDIC contracts, particularly programme, progress, delay and claims provisions. Solid understanding of CPM scheduling, WBS, progress measurement and EVM. UAE or GCC rail experience, such as Etihad Rail, Dubai Metro or similar programmes. Experience with multi-contract programmes and interface management. Experience with schedule risk analysis tools and Power BI reporting.
